newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian chief says rebels under control.
newsitem.headline: Colombian chief says rebels under control.

text.p: Colombian President Ernesto Samper announced on Monday three new measures to combat left-wing guerrillas amid fears that rebel violence is spiraling out of control.
In an interview with El Tiempo, Colombia's leading daily, Samper said military intelligence would be stepped up, communication links boosted and troop mobility by land, air and river improved.
Despite clashes that have taken the lives of more than 110 soldiers, police, insurgents and civilians across the country in the last 10 days, Samper insisted the situation was under control.

"The government is aware of the seriousness of the situation but at this time we are in control of the situation despite all the difficulties. We have suffered casualties but so have the guerrillas," he said.

But in the southern province of Putumayo, site of some of the worst fighting in more than three decades of guerrilla war, Gov. Jorge Fuerbringer said the left-wing Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia (FARC) were virtually laying siege to the capital, Mocoa.

He told the Caracol radio network on Monday: "It's not out of the question (that guerrillas could attack the capital), they are very close. The situation is quite worrying -- neither fuel to generate electricity nor provisions are coming into the state. Business has been devastated."
FARC rebels overran a military base in Las Delicias in the southeast of the province on Aug. 30, killing more than 30 soldiers and kidnapping 67.

In a communique sent to the International Red Cross early on Monday rebel leaders denied any soliders had been tortured. They have said they will free the soldiers only if the release zone is demilitarized three days before and have called for international representatives to witness the handover.
One of the major problems said to be facing the Colombian military is its lack of mobility. The army has only about 35 helicopters to transport ground troops to conflict zones.
